work.title: The Third Part of King Henry the Sixth
work.author: William Shakespeare

content.text: Flourish. March. Enter Queen Margaret, Prince Edward, Somerset, Oxford and Soldiers.

lines.text: Great lords, wise men ne'er sit and wail their loss,
lines.plainText: Great lords wise men ne'er sit and wail their loss

lines.text: But cheerly seek how to redress their harms.
lines.plainText: But cheerly seek how to redress their harms

lines.text: What though the mast be now blown overboard,
lines.plainText: What though the mast be now blown overboard

lines.text: The cable broke, the holding-anchor lost,
lines.plainText: The cable broke the holdinganchor lost

lines.text: And half our sailors swallowed in the flood?
lines.plainText: And half our sailors swallowed in the flood

lines.text: Yet lives our pilot still. Is 't meet that he
lines.plainText: Yet lives our pilot still Is 't meet that he

lines.text: Should leave the helm and, like a fearful lad,
lines.plainText: Should leave the helm and like a fearful lad

lines.text: With tearful eyes add water to the sea
lines.plainText: With tearful eyes add water to the sea

lines.text: And give more strength to that which hath too much,
lines.plainText: And give more strength to that which hath too much

lines.text: Whiles in his moan the ship splits on the rock,
lines.plainText: Whiles in his moan the ship splits on the rock

lines.text: Which industry and courage might have saved?
lines.plainText: Which industry and courage might have saved

lines.text: Ah, what a shame, ah, what a fault were this!
lines.plainText: Ah what a shame ah what a fault were this

lines.text: Say Warwick was our anchor; what of that?
lines.plainText: Say Warwick was our anchor what of that

lines.text: And Montague our topmast; what of him?
lines.plainText: And Montague our topmast what of him

lines.text: Our slaughtered friends the tackles; what of these?
lines.plainText: Our slaughtered friends the tackles what of these

lines.text: Why, is not Oxford here another anchor?
lines.plainText: Why is not Oxford here another anchor

lines.text: And Somerset another goodly mast?
lines.plainText: And Somerset another goodly mast

lines.text: The friends of France our shrouds and tacklings?
lines.plainText: The friends of France our shrouds and tacklings

lines.text: And, though unskilful, why not Ned and I
lines.plainText: And though unskilful why not Ned and I

lines.text: For once allowed the skilful pilot's charge?
lines.plainText: For once allowed the skilful pilot's charge

lines.text: We will not from the helm to sit and weep,
lines.plainText: We will not from the helm to sit and weep

lines.text: But keep our course, though the rough wind say no,
lines.plainText: But keep our course though the rough wind say no

lines.text: From shelves and rocks that threaten us with wrack.
lines.plainText: From shelves and rocks that threaten us with wrack

lines.text: As good to chide the waves as speak them fair.
lines.plainText: As good to chide the waves as speak them fair

lines.text: And what is Edward but a ruthless sea?
lines.plainText: And what is Edward but a ruthless sea

lines.text: What Clarence but a quicksand of deceit?
lines.plainText: What Clarence but a quicksand of deceit

lines.text: And Richard but a ragged fatal rock?
lines.plainText: And Richard but a ragged fatal rock

lines.text: All these the enemies to our poor bark?
lines.plainText: All these the enemies to our poor bark

lines.text: Say you can swim: alas, 'tis but a while!
lines.plainText: Say you can swim alas 'tis but a while

lines.text: Tread on the sand: why, there you quickly sink;
lines.plainText: Tread on the sand why there you quickly sink

lines.text: Bestride the rock: the tide will wash you off,
lines.plainText: Bestride the rock the tide will wash you off

lines.text: Or else you famish; that's a threefold death.
lines.plainText: Or else you famish that's a threefold death

lines.text: This speak I, lords, to let you understand,
lines.plainText: This speak I lords to let you understand

lines.text: If case some one of you would fly from us,
lines.plainText: If case some one of you would fly from us

lines.text: That there's no hoped-for mercy with the brothers
lines.plainText: That there's no hopedfor mercy with the brothers

lines.text: More than with ruthless waves, with sands, and rocks.
lines.plainText: More than with ruthless waves with sands and rocks

lines.text: Why, courage then! What cannot be avoided
lines.plainText: Why courage then What cannot be avoided

lines.text: 'Twere childish weakness to lament or fear.
lines.plainText: 'Twere childish weakness to lament or fear

lines.text: Methinks a woman of this valiant spirit
lines.plainText: Methinks a woman of this valiant spirit

lines.text: Should, if a coward heard her speak these words,
lines.plainText: Should if a coward heard her speak these words

lines.text: Infuse his breast with magnanimity
lines.plainText: Infuse his breast with magnanimity

lines.text: And make him, naked, foil a man at arms.
lines.plainText: And make him naked foil a man at arms

lines.text: I speak not this as doubting any here;
lines.plainText: I speak not this as doubting any here

lines.text: For did I but suspect a fearful man,
lines.plainText: For did I but suspect a fearful man

lines.text: He should have leave to go away betimes,
lines.plainText: He should have leave to go away betimes

lines.text: Lest in our need he might infect another
lines.plainText: Lest in our need he might infect another

lines.text: And make him of the like spirit to himself.
lines.plainText: And make him of the like spirit to himself

lines.text: If any such be here, as God forbid!
lines.plainText: If any such be here as God forbid

lines.text: Let him depart before we need his help.
lines.plainText: Let him depart before we need his help

lines.text: Women and children of so high a courage,
lines.plainText: Women and children of so high a courage

lines.text: And warriors faint! Why, 'twere perpetual shame.
lines.plainText: And warriors faint Why 'twere perpetual shame

lines.text: O, brave young Prince, thy famous grandfather
lines.plainText: O brave young Prince thy famous grandfather

lines.text: Doth live again in thee. Long mayst thou live
lines.plainText: Doth live again in thee Long mayst thou live

lines.text: To bear his image and renew his glories!
lines.plainText: To bear his image and renew his glories

lines.text: And he that will not fight for such a hope,
lines.plainText: And he that will not fight for such a hope

lines.text: Go home to bed and, like the owl by day,
lines.plainText: Go home to bed and like the owl by day

lines.text: If he arise, be mocked and wondered at.
lines.plainText: If he arise be mocked and wondered at

lines.text: Thanks, gentle Somerset. Sweet Oxford, thanks.
lines.plainText: Thanks gentle Somerset Sweet Oxford thanks

lines.text: And take his thanks that yet hath nothing else.
lines.plainText: And take his thanks that yet hath nothing else

lines.text: Prepare you, lords, for Edward is at hand
lines.plainText: Prepare you lords for Edward is at hand

lines.text: Ready to fight; therefore be resolute.
lines.plainText: Ready to fight therefore be resolute

lines.text: I thought no less. It is his policy
lines.plainText: I thought no less It is his policy

lines.text: To haste thus fast, to find us unprovided.
lines.plainText: To haste thus fast to find us unprovided

lines.text: But he's deceived; we are in readiness.
lines.plainText: But he's deceived we are in readiness

lines.text: This cheers my heart, to see your forwardness.
lines.plainText: This cheers my heart to see your forwardness

lines.text: Here pitch our battle; hence we will not budge.
lines.plainText: Here pitch our battle hence we will not budge

content.text: Flourish and march. Enter King Edward, Richard, George and Soldiers.

lines.text: Brave followers, yonder stands the thorny wood
lines.plainText: Brave followers yonder stands the thorny wood

lines.text: Which by the heaven's assistance and your strength
lines.plainText: Which by the heaven's assistance and your strength

lines.text: Must by the roots be hewn up yet ere night.
lines.plainText: Must by the roots be hewn up yet ere night

lines.text: I need not add more fuel to your fire,
lines.plainText: I need not add more fuel to your fire

lines.text: For, well I wot, ye blaze to burn them out.
lines.plainText: For well I wot ye blaze to burn them out

lines.text: Give signal to the fight, and to it, lords!
lines.plainText: Give signal to the fight and to it lords

lines.text: Lords, knights, and gentlemen, what I should say
lines.plainText: Lords knights and gentlemen what I should say

lines.text: My tears gainsay; for every word I speak
lines.plainText: My tears gainsay for every word I speak

lines.text: Ye see I drink the water of my eye.
lines.plainText: Ye see I drink the water of my eye

lines.text: Therefore, no more but this: Henry, your sovereign,
lines.plainText: Therefore no more but this Henry your sovereign

lines.text: Is prisoner to the foe, his state usurped,
lines.plainText: Is prisoner to the foe his state usurped

lines.text: His realm a slaughter-house, his subjects slain,
lines.plainText: His realm a slaughterhouse his subjects slain

lines.text: His statutes cancelled, and his treasure spent;
lines.plainText: His statutes cancelled and his treasure spent

lines.text: And yonder is the wolf that makes this spoil.
lines.plainText: And yonder is the wolf that makes this spoil

lines.text: You fight in justice. Then, in God's name, lords,
lines.plainText: You fight in justice Then in God's name lords

lines.text: Be valiant and give signal to the fight.
lines.plainText: Be valiant and give signal to the fight
